info.title: Power Platform Licensing API
info.version: v0.1-alpha + v1.0 + v2.0 (three coexisting route prefixes; see info.x-versioning)
info.description:
The Power Platform licensing service reports tenant capacity, entitlements, billing policies and per-user trials.

Its versioning is unusual: the version is a **path segment** (`v0.1-alpha`, `v1.0`, `v2.0`) rather than an `api-version` parameter, registration is per route, and where a route serves several segments the representations can differ substantially.

For most purposes prefer the Power Platform API's `/licensing` operations, which are documented and coherently versioned; this service is worth reaching for only where it exposes something they do not.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/licensing) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

x-versioning.description: The `/{segment}/` prefix is a literal route segment, not an api-version.
evidence: Every route on this host, whatever its segment, reports `api-supported-versions: 1.0`.

`GET /v2.0/tenants/{tenantId}/BillingPolicies?api-version=1.0` returns 200; `?api-version=2.0` returns 400 with an empty body. The segment and the query parameter are independent, and only `1.0` is a valid api-version anywhere.
`Users/{userId}/Trials` advertises `api-supported-versions: 1.0, 2`, yet `?api-version=2` is rejected with 400. The advertised set is not honoured.
An `api-version` request *header*, and `Accept: application/json;v=2.0`, are both ignored.
Route matching -- including the version segment itself -- is case-insensitive: `/V2.0/tenants/{id}/billingpolicies` returns the same 200 as `/v2.0/tenants/{id}/BillingPolicies`.

IsvContracts: v1.0 -- route exists but answered 403 on a tenant with no ISV contracts, so no body was observed and it is not documented as an operation

representationsDiffer: `BillingPolicies` under `v0.1-alpha` models pay-as-you-go as five per-product policy objects with `Enabled`/`Disabled` strings; under `v2.0` the same policy is a flat `payGoEntitlements` array of booleans. Same records, incompatible models.

`Entitlements/{id}` under `v0.1-alpha` returns scalar `capacity.entitled`/`capacity.consumed`; under `v2.0` those are boxed objects and the response gains `allocated`, `availableQuantity` and `status`.
`Users/{userId}/Trials` under `v0.1-alpha` returns dates only; under `v1.0` the same trial gains `trialCurrencyUnits` and `trialCount`.
representationsIdentical: `Environments/{environmentId}/BillingPolicy` returns the `v2.0` billing-policy representation on all three segments, including `v0.1-alpha`.

x-error-envelopes.description: Five unrelated error shapes are emitted by one host. Branch on the status code and then on the JSON's top-level type.

problemDetails.observedOn: 404 on a route that exists but whose bound id has no record -- an environment with no currency allocation, an unknown environment under a billing policy, a recognised entitlement id the tenant holds no entitlement for.
problemDetails.note: RFC 9110 section 15.5.5. `traceId` is an ASP.NET Core connection/request id, not a correlation id a caller can hand to support.

nestedErrorWithDetails.observedOn: 400 when a path segment fails enum binding -- `Trials/{trialType}` with anything other than `AI`.
nestedErrorWithDetails.note: `target` names the offending route parameter, which makes this the only envelope a caller can act on programmatically.

keyMessageArray.observedOn: 404 on `Entitlements/{entitlementId}` when the id is not a value the entitlement subsystem recognises at all.
keyMessageArray.note: A bare JSON array, not an object. `message` interpolates the tenant id into free text ('<id> - <tenantId> is not valid').

serviceFabricError.observedOn: 500 when a route parameter cannot be bound at all -- a non-GUID user id, or `Trials/0`.
serviceFabricError.note: `namespace` was `CoreFramework` and `code` `UnknownError` in every instance; a binding failure surfacing as a 500 rather than a 400.

emptyBody.observedOn: 401, 403, 405, 400 on `?api-version`, and 404 on a route this host does not recognise.
emptyBody.note: The commonest outcome. Because an unrecognised route also answers 404 with an empty body, a caller cannot tell 'no such route' from 'forbidden' by the body alone -- see `info.x-route-existence-oracle`.

x-write-surface.description: Every method each route accepts, mapped without issuing a single mutating request. HEAD is refused with 405 on every route on this host, and the Allow header that comes back enumerates the methods the route does accept. Nothing below was invoked and nothing below is documented as an operation, because the request and response bodies were never seen.
x-write-surface.method: HEAD against each route; read the Allow header of the 405.
x-write-surface.readsThis: Five routes take writes: create and update/delete a billing policy, refresh its provisioning status, PATCH environment currency allocations, and POST a user trial (which is how a trial is started). The Allow values match the shape of the equivalent Power Platform API operations -- `POST /licensing/billingPolicies`, `PUT`/`DELETE /licensing/billingPolicies/{id}`, `PATCH /licensing/allocationsByEnvironment` -- which is further evidence the two hosts front the same service.
x-write-surface.notDocumented: None of these is written up as an operation here. `scripts/probe.py` refuses every method but GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, so no body was ever observed and guessing one from the ppapi models would be an invention. Use [ppapi](spec:ppapi) for writes; it documents them and the Terraform provider exercises them.
x-write-surface.absent: `BillingPolicies/{id}/Environments/add` and `.../remove`, which ppapi exposes, are **not** routes here: they bind as `{environmentId}` on the GET route instead, which is why they answer 404 with problem details rather than 405.

x-route-existence-oracle.description: How to tell a route that exists from one that does not, given that both can answer 404 with an empty body.
x-route-existence-oracle.test: The `api-supported-versions` response header is present if and only if the request matched a registered route. A 404 carrying `api-supported-versions: 1.0` means the route exists and the bound id has no record; a 404 without it means this host has no such route.
x-route-existence-oracle.corollary: `x-servicefabric: ResourceNotFound` accompanies both and is not a discriminator.
x-route-existence-oracle.falsePositive: `GET /` answers 200 with a vestigial, empty OData service document, and `GET /$metadata` with an EDMX containing an empty entity container. Neither is part of this API; both will fool a probe that treats 200 as evidence.

x-sovereign-hosts.description: The seven hostnames the Terraform provider declares for this API, and what each resolves to. Recorded because the provider is the only published source for them and it never calls any of them.
x-sovereign-hosts.provenance: internal/constants/constants.go lines 33 (PUBLIC), 47 (USDOD), 61 (USGOV), 75 (USGOVHIGH), 89 (CHINA), 104 (EX), 119 (RX) of microsoft/terraform-provider-power-platform, pinned by internal/constants/constants_test.go.
x-sovereign-hosts.namingIsNotUniform: Three patterns, not one. The US Government clouds keep the commercial domain and prefix the geo (`gov.`, `high.`); DoD, China and both air-gapped clouds change the entire domain (`licensing.appsplatform.us`, `licensing.partner.microsoftonline.cn`, `licensing.eaglex.ic.gov`, `licensing.microsoft.scloud`). A caller cannot compose these from the commercial host by string substitution.

dnsVerified2026_08_27.gov.licensing.powerplatform.microsoft.us: CNAME nptn-gcc-tm.usgovtrafficmanager.net -> Azure Front Door (US Gov).
dnsVerified2026_08_27.high.licensing.powerplatform.microsoft.u: CNAME nptn-usg-tm.usgovtrafficmanager.net -> Azure Front Door (US Gov).
dnsVerified2026_08_27.licensing.appsplatform.us: CNAME nptn-dod-tm.usgovtrafficmanager.net -> Azure Front Door (US Gov).

x-sovereign-hosts.note: Every resolvable host fronts a Traffic Manager profile named `nptn-<cloud>-tm`, and the China chain names the origin outright: the service's internal codename is **Neptune**. That is the only self-identification this host offers -- there is no service document, no health endpoint and no version endpoint.

x-relationship-to-power-platform-api.description: How this host relates to `api.powerplatform.com/licensing` (the ppapi spec in this repo), which is the surface Microsoft documents and the Terraform provider actually calls.

sameResources.entitlements: here `/{segment}/tenants/{tenantId}/Entitlements[/{entitlementId}]`; on ppapi `/licensing/entitlements/{entitlementId}` and its consumption sub-resources.
sameResources.ISV contracts: `/v1.0/tenants/{tenantId}/IsvContracts` exists here and answers 403 for a tenant with no ISV contracts; on ppapi it is `/licensing/isvContracts`.

differences: **Tenant addressing.** Every route here names the tenant in the path. ppapi takes the tenant from the token and has no tenant segment at all.
**Versioning.** ppapi uses a single `?api-version=2022-03-01-preview` query parameter throughout. Here the version is a literal path segment, and the query parameter is a trap (`400`).
**Audience.** Distinct Entra resources. A token for `https://api.powerplatform.com/.default` is rejected here with `401 Bearer error="invalid_token"`, and vice versa.
**Richer records.** The `v2.0` billing policy here carries `type`, `payGoEntitlements[]` and `billingInstrument.provisioningStatus`; ppapi's `BillingPolicyResponseModel` carries none of the three.

**Write surface.** Both hosts take writes on the same resources -- `info.x-write-surface` maps this one from Allow headers -- but ppapi documents its request bodies and this one does not, so nothing here is written up as a mutation. ppapi additionally has `environments/add` and `environments/remove`, which are not routes on this host at all.
x-relationship-to-power-platform-api.whichToUse: Prefer ppapi. It is documented on Microsoft Learn, versioned coherently, tenant-scoped by token, and it is what the Terraform provider calls. Reach for this host only for what ppapi does not expose -- the per-product `v0.1-alpha` policy representation, `payGoEntitlements`, `billingInstrument.provisioningStatus`, and per-user trials -- or when reading a tenant other than the token's own.

x-notes.note:
**Eleven further routes are known to exist on this host but are not modelled as operations here**, because the only evidence for them is that a discovery script tried them. Nothing in the source that names them parses a response, so there is nothing to say about what they return, and modelling them would put entries in this spec whose sole content is a path someone guessed:

`GET /v0.1/tenants/{tenantId}/allocationsV2/sum`, `POST /v0.1/tenants/{tenantId}/allocationsV2/getmany` (seen with an empty body and with `{startDate,endDate}`), `POST /v0.1/tenants/{tenantId}/allocationsV2/overage/getmany`, `GET /v0.1/tenants/{tenantId}/ManagedEnvironment/PowerApps/GetLicenseSummary`, `GET /v0.1-alpha/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements/extension`, `GET /v2.0/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements/MCSMessages`, `GET /v0.1-alpha/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements/MCSMessages/snapshot/resources` (`startDate`, `endDate`), `GET /v0.1-alpha/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements/MCSMessages/snapshot/product`, `GET /v0.1-alpha/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements/MCSMessages/trends` (`from`, `to`), `GET /v1.0/tenants/{tenantId}/capacityTypes/MCSMessages/trends`.

They are recorded because knowing a route exists is worth something to whoever probes next, and because their shape is informative on its own: `allocationsV2` reads in bulk through POST rather than GET, and the MCSMessages family spans three version prefixes at once.

**Four version families are live on this host simultaneously** -- `v0.1-alpha`, `v0.1`, `v1.0` and `v2.0` -- and they are not successive generations of one surface. `CurrencyReports` exists at both `v0.1-alpha` and `v1.0`; `MCSMessages` entitlements appear under `v0.1-alpha` and `v2.0`; `allocationsV2` sits alone on `v0.1`. The prefix is part of the route rather than a version of the API, so a client cannot pick one and use it throughout.

servers.description: Commercial cloud. `PUBLIC_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. The only host probed; everything marked `x-probe-verified` was verified here.
US Government Community Cloud (GCC). `USGOV_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. Resolves; not probed -- a commercial-cloud token has the wrong audience.
US Government GCC High. `USGOVHIGH_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. Resolves; not probed.
US Department of Defense. `USDOD_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. Resolves; not probed. Note the whole domain changes rather than gaining a `dod.` prefix.
US Air-Gapped Cloud (EX). `EX_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. Not publicly resolvable, as expected for an air-gapped cloud; unverifiable from the internet.
US Air-Gapped Cloud (RX). `RX_LICENSING_API_DOMAIN`. Not publicly resolvable; unverifiable from the internet.

tags.name: Allocations V2
tags.description: A second-generation allocation surface addressed with bulk reads. Distinct from the `allocationsByEnvironment` routes, and on its own `v0.1` version family.

tags.name: Billing Policy
tags.description: A pay-as-you-go billing policy: the object that links a set of Power Platform environments to an Azure subscription so that consumption beyond the tenant's licensed capacity is billed to that subscription rather than blocked. A policy names the Azure billing instrument, the geography it may cover, and which product meters are switched into pay-as-you-go. See [Pay-as-you-go overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-overview).

tags.name: Billing Policy to Environment link
tags.description: The many-to-one association between environments and a billing policy. An environment has at most one policy; a policy covers any number of environments in its geography. The link is readable from either side, and the two sides live on different route shapes.

tags.name: Copilot Studio Messages
tags.description: Capacity for Copilot Studio messages (`MCSMessages`), the consumption currency Copilot Studio bills against. Reported per environment, per agent resource and per user, as snapshots and as trends.

tags.name: Currency Allocation
tags.description: Power Platform *currencies* -- prepaid unit pools such as Windows 365 pay-as-you-go hours or AI Builder credits -- and how a tenant's purchased units are distributed to environments. A currency is purchased at tenant level and then allocated; unallocated units sit in the tenant pool.

tags.name: Entitlement
tags.description: A single metered resource the tenant is entitled to -- storage in megabytes, API calls, Windows 365 pay-as-you-go hours -- with what was purchased, what has been consumed, what has been allocated to environments, and which licences contribute to it. This is the per-meter view; *Tenant Capacity* is the same information rolled up.

tags.name: Service Root
tags.description: A vestigial OData surface mounted at the host root. It is not part of the licensing API and exposes no data, but it answers `200`, so route discovery that treats a `200` as a live endpoint will be misled by it.

tags.name: Tenant Capacity
tags.description: The tenant-wide capacity rollup that backs the admin center's *Capacity* page: every storage and count meter, its entitlement, its measured consumption, the licences that granted it, and an overall status summary. Consumption figures are snapshots refreshed on a schedule, not live counters.

tags.name: User Trial
tags.description: A per-user product trial: a time-boxed grant of a currency to one user, with its start and expiry and how much of the granted allowance has been consumed. Read by the maker portal to decide whether to offer trial-backed features to the signed-in user.

get.description:
Reads one environment's currency allocations.

A 404 is the ordinary answer, not a fault: the route matched and the environment simply has nothing allocated. First-party UI calls this speculatively for the environment being edited and reads the 404 as 'nothing allocated'.

The two failure modes differ. An environment this service can resolve but that holds no allocation answers problem-details `404`. An id it cannot resolve answers `403` with an empty body, and that covers both ids from outside the tenant and environments provisioned too recently for this service to see — so a `403` here means 'not visible to this service, yet or at all' rather than a clean permission verdict.

Purchased, allocated and consumed quantities per currency type for the tenant. A `v1.0` sibling of the `v0.1-alpha` route of the same name, and the version the admin centre calls.

**The response is polymorphic**: it is sometimes a bare JSON array and sometimes an object wrapping that array in `value`. A client must test which it received -- Microsoft's own consumer does exactly that.

get.description:
Lists every product trial the named user has taken, with its currency allowances and how much of each has been spent. The maker portal calls this to decide whether to offer trial-backed features to the signed-in user.

The path also accepts `POST` (`Allow: GET, POST`), which is presumably how a trial is started. It was not invoked and its body is not documented.

x-notes.note: The list is not filtered to usable trials. Expired ones are returned alongside live ones, so a caller compares `expiryDate` against the current time itself; and a trial can be spent before it expires, when `trialConsumedUnits` reaches `trialUnits`.

Lists every pay-as-you-go billing policy in the tenant, richest representation first.

Unpaged and unfiltered: there is no `nextLink` and no continuation token, and `$top` -- along with any other query parameter -- is accepted and ignored.

This path also accepts `POST` (`Allow: GET, POST`), and the item path `PUT` and `DELETE`, so policies can be created and changed here -- but no request body was ever observed and none is documented. Prefer the [Power Platform API](spec:ppapi) for writes, and for reads too unless you specifically need `type`, `payGoEntitlements` or `billingInstrument.provisioningStatus`, none of which it returns.

get.description:

The id vocabulary is narrower than it looks. Of the eleven `entitlementId` values a billing policy enumerates, only `Database`, `File`, `Log` and `W365APAYGO` resolve; the rest 404. Worse, they 404 in two different shapes -- some return problem details and some return the bare `[{key, message}]` array -- so the two vocabularies overlap only partially and a client cannot reuse ids across the two subsystems.

Two unrelated bodies are returned here: problem details when the id is one the entitlement subsystem recognises but the tenant does not hold, and a bare `[{key, message}]` array when the id is not recognised at all. Branch on the JSON's top-level type.

get.description:
Message consumption per agent resource, across **every environment in one call** rather than per environment. Each row carries the environment, the resource, what it consumed and the unit, with the resource's name and any non-billable quantity under `metadata`.

The caller must hold Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator. Anything less is refused with `403` rather than an empty result.

200.description: Fields observed being read by Microsoft's own consumer: `resources`, `environmentId`, `resourceId`, `consumed`, `unit`, `metadata.ResourceName`, `metadata.NonBillableQuantity`, `asOfDate`.

403.description: The caller is not a Power Platform or Global Administrator.

get.description:
Message consumption per user over an explicit window. **The window is mandatory** -- unlike the resource route, this one does not default to a period, and `fromDate` and `toDate` must both be supplied.

The caller must hold Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator. Anything less is refused with `403` rather than an empty result.

200.description: Fields observed being read by Microsoft's own consumer: `value`, `users`, `tenantId`, `userId`, `consumed`, `unit`, `metadata.Resources`, `metadata.NonBillableQuantity`, `asOfDate`.

403.description: The caller is not a Power Platform or Global Administrator.

get.description:
Message capacity and consumption per environment.

**The capacity object is not uniformly shaped**: `allocated` and `consumed` are wrapped objects carrying a `value`, while `availableQuantity` beside them is a bare scalar. A client that treats the three alike will read an object where it expects a number.

The caller must hold Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator. Anything less is refused with `403` rather than an empty result.

200.description: Fields observed being read by Microsoft's own consumer: `value`, `environmentId`, `environmentName`, `entitlement.capacity.allocated.value`, `entitlement.capacity.consumed.value`, `entitlement.capacity.availableQuantity`.

403.description: The caller is not a Power Platform or Global Administrator.

azure_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID. The scope is `https://licensing.powerplatform.microsoft.com/.default`, a resource of its own: the delegated token it mints carries `aud: https://licensing.powerplatform.microsoft.com` and the single legacy scope `user_impersonation` -- there are no granular scopes to request, so any token that works here works for the whole surface. A token for `https://api.powerplatform.com/.default` is rejected with 401 even though that API serves the same resources under `/licensing/`.

scopes.https://licensing.powerplatform.microsof: Read the tenant's licensing position: entitlements, capacity, billing policies, currency allocations and user trials

billingPolicyId.name: billingPolicyId
billingPolicyId.description: Billing policy id, as returned by the list operation.

entitlementId.name: entitlementId
entitlementId.description: The metered resource to read. Matched case-insensitively. This vocabulary is **not** the one `BillingPolicy.payGoEntitlements[].entitlementId` uses: of the eleven ids a billing policy lists, only `Database`, `File`, `Log` and `W365APAYGO` resolve here.

environmentId.name: environmentId
environmentId.description: Power Platform environment id -- the same id BAPI and the Power Platform API use, not the Dataverse organization id.

tenantId.name: tenantId
tenantId.description: Entra tenant whose licensing position is being read. Unlike the Power Platform API, this service does *not* take the tenant from the token: it must be named in the path, and it must match the token's tenant -- any other value, including a malformed one, answers 403 with an empty body.

trialType.name: trialType
trialType.description: Which trial to read. Bound as a .NET enum: matched case-insensitively, tolerant of trailing whitespace, and also accepted as the ordinal `1`. `AI` is the only name that binds.

userId.name: userId
userId.description: Entra object id of the user. Must be a well-formed GUID: anything else is a 500, not a 400.

AllocatedQuantity.description: How much of a tenant-level entitlement has been handed down to environments. Only the v2.0 representation reports allocation.

autoAllocated.description: The part of `value` the service assigned by itself rather than an administrator, under auto-allocation.

BillingInstrument.description: The Azure resource that consumption under this policy is billed to: a `Microsoft.PowerPlatform/accounts` resource in the tenant's own Azure subscription. Deleting or moving that Azure resource is what breaks a billing policy, which is why `provisioningStatus` is reported alongside it.

id.description: Full Azure resource id of the `Microsoft.PowerPlatform/accounts` resource. Composed from the other two fields plus the account name, which the API does not return separately -- the account name is the trailing segment.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group holding the account resource.

subscriptionId.description: Azure subscription that receives the charges. It must belong to the same tenant.

provisioningStatus.description: State of the underlying Azure resource as the licensing service last saw it. A policy whose instrument is not `Succeeded` will not bill. This field has no counterpart in the ppapi representation of the same record.
provisioningStatus.x-enum-evidence: Both policies in the probed tenant were `Succeeded`. Azure provisioning states (`Failed`, `Accepted`, `Deleting`) are the obvious rest of the set but were not observed, so no `enum` is asserted.

BillingPolicy.description: A pay-as-you-go billing policy in the v2.0 representation: metadata, the Azure billing instrument, and a flat array of per-meter pay-as-you-go switches. This is the richer of the two representations the host offers and the one to prefer.

name.description: Administrator-chosen name. Not unique and not an identifier; it is also the trailing segment of the Azure account resource id in `billingInstrument.id`.

type.description: Who owns the policy. A tenant's own policies bill to that tenant's Azure subscription; an ISV-owned policy bills a publisher instead.
type.x-enum-evidence: Only `TenantOwned` was observed; the probed tenant has no ISV contracts. The field is absent from the ppapi representation entirely.

status.description: Whether the policy is currently billing. A disabled policy keeps its environment links but stops absorbing overage.
status.x-enum-evidence: `Enabled` observed live; `Disabled` from the ppapi `BillingPolicyStatus` schema for the same record.

location.description: Power Platform geography the policy may cover. An environment can only be linked to a policy in its own geography, so this is a hard constraint on the environment link operations, not a label.

BillingPolicyEnvironment.description: One environment's membership of a billing policy. The record carries nothing but the two ids -- no environment name, no state, no date the link was made -- so it is a join row, not a resource with substance.

BillingPolicyList.description: Envelope around the tenant's billing policies. There is no paging: no `nextLink`, no continuation token, and `$top` is accepted and ignored.

BillingPolicyProductView.description: The same billing policy record as `BillingPolicy`, in the v0.1-alpha representation: pay-as-you-go is modelled as five per-product objects carrying `Enabled`/`Disabled` strings rather than one flat array of booleans. Neither model is a subset of the other -- v0.1-alpha groups the three Power Automate meters and drops the three Dataverse meters into a single `storagePolicy`, while v2.0 lists all eleven meters individually but loses the grouping.

status.description: Whether the policy is currently billing.

location.description: Power Platform geography the policy may cover.

powerAppsPolicy.description: Power Apps app passes. Corresponds to the `AppPass` entitlement in the v2.0 representation.

storagePolicy.description: Dataverse storage. One switch here corresponds to *three* v2.0 entitlements -- `Database`, `File` and `Log` -- which the service keeps in lockstep.

powerPagesPolicy.description: Power Pages. One switch here covers both the `PowerPagesAuthenticated` and `PowerPagesAnonymous` v2.0 entitlements.

powerVirtualAgentPolicy.description: Copilot Studio (formerly Power Virtual Agents) messages. Corresponds to `MCSMessages`. Note there is no v0.1-alpha counterpart for the `W365APAYGO` entitlement at all.

BillingPolicyProductViewList.description: Envelope around the tenant's billing policies in the v0.1-alpha representation. Unpaged, like its v2.0 twin.

CapacityConsumption.description: What has actually been used against a meter.

x-notes.note: Neither figure is a live counter. Both are periodically refreshed snapshots, and their timestamps were identical across every meter in one response, so the whole rollup is computed in a single scheduled pass.

actual.description: Raw measured consumption in the meter's `capacityUnits`.

rated.description: Consumption after the service's own rating rules -- the figure billing and overage decisions use. It can be far below `actual` (observed roughly one tenth for file storage), so comparing `actual` against entitlement will overstate overage.

CapacityEntitlement.description: One layer of a meter's entitlement. A meter's total is the sum of its layers: a `...Base` layer from the tenant's baseline grant, an `...Incremental` layer accruing per licensed user, and an `...AddOn` layer from separately purchased capacity packs. Layers with no licences still appear, with `totalCapacity` zero.

capacitySubType.description: Which layer this is. The suffix is the meaning: `Base` is the tenant baseline, `Incremental` accrues per licensed user, `AddOn` is purchased capacity.
capacitySubType.x-enum-evidence: The full set emitted across all sixteen meters of one tenant's rollup; the service lists every layer it models, including empty ones.

totalCapacity.description: Capacity this layer contributes, in the parent meter's `capacityUnits`.

licenses.description: The licences that produced this layer. Empty for baseline layers a tenant holds by default.

CapacityLicense.description: One licence SKU contributing storage or count capacity to the tenant, as reported by the capacity rollup. This is a different shape from the licence record returned under an entitlement -- the two subsystems do not share a model.

entitlementCode.description: Microsoft's internal service-plan code for the grant, which is what actually identifies the capacity source; the SKU alone does not.

x-notes.note: Empty for every licence observed, despite the name. `EntitlementLicense.productName` is the field that actually carries a friendly name.

servicePlanId.description: Entra service-plan id, joinable against Microsoft Graph `subscribedSkus`.

skuId.description: Entra SKU id the service plan belongs to.

paid.description: Seat counts for purchased licences of this SKU.

trial.description: Seat counts for trial licences of this SKU, counted separately because trial capacity expires.

totalCapacity.description: Capacity this licence grants, in the parent meter's `capacityUnits`.

capabilityStatus.description: Whether the grant is currently in force.

CapacitySummary.description: Tenant-wide capacity verdict, and the text the admin center shows above the capacity table. The message strings are prose meant for display; the `...Code` fields are what to branch on.

statusMessage.description: Display sentence explaining `status`, already localised for the caller.
statusMessage.example: Database, Log and File storage are over capacity. This will impact certain environment operations.

statusMessageCode.description: Stable code behind `statusMessage`. Branch on this, not on the prose.

finOpsStatus.description: Separate verdict for Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations storage, which is reported alongside but not folded into `status`.

finOpsStatusMessage.description: Display sentence for the Finance and Operations verdict.

ConsumedQuantity.description: A consumed amount together with how it was measured.

value.description: Amount consumed, in the entitlement's unit.

consumptionType.description: How the figure is derived. `Snapshot` is a point-in-time measurement of a stock (storage in use); `NotSpecified` is returned for meters measured as a flow, where the value is a running total.

lastUpdatedOn.description: When the snapshot was taken. Absent on `NotSpecified` meters.

writeOff.description: Consumption Microsoft has waived and will not bill or count against entitlement.

CurrencyReport.description: Purchase and allocation position for one Power Platform currency at tenant level. `purchased - allocated` is what is left in the tenant pool for new environment allocations.

currencyType.x-enum-evidence: `W365APAYGO` from the currency report of the probed tenant, `AI` from a trial record on the same tenant. The full vocabulary is larger and was not enumerable -- the service reports only currencies the tenant holds.

allocated.description: Units already handed to environments. Never exceeds `purchased`.

Entitlement.description: One metered resource the tenant is entitled to, in the v2.0 representation.

productCategories.description: Products this meter belongs to. Returned empty for the storage meters and populated for product-specific ones, so an empty array does not mean 'unknown'.

entitlement.description: The two sides of the meter, licensed and pay-as-you-go.

EntitlementCapacity.description: The licensed side of an entitlement in the v2.0 representation: what was granted, what is used, what is allocated, and what is left.

unit.description: Unit for the quantities here. Repeated from the parent, and observed to disagree with it: the parent reported `Count` for a meter whose capacity block said `NotSpecified`.

availableQuantity.description: Entitlement still free, after consumption and allocation.

status.description: Whether the meter is inside its entitlement.
status.x-enum-evidence: Both values observed live -- `WithinCapacity` on an unused meter, `Overage` on storage past its grant.

licenses.description: Licences contributing the entitlement. Can be empty on a storage meter even where the entitlement itself is non-zero.

EntitlementFlatCapacity.description: The licensed side of an entitlement in the v0.1-alpha representation: bare numbers where v2.0 boxes them, and no `allocated`, `availableQuantity` or `status` at all.

consumed.description: Amount used. Where v2.0 attaches a measurement type and timestamp, this representation gives the number alone.

EntitlementLicense.description: One licence contributing to an entitlement. Note this is a different shape from `CapacityLicense`, which describes the same underlying idea for the capacity rollup: the field names, the quantity model and the status vocabulary all differ.

productName.description: Friendly SKU name. Unlike `CapacityLicense.displayName` this is actually populated.

licenseQuantity.description: Seats held. Equals the sum of `licenseQuantityDetails`.

entitled.description: Capacity these seats grant, in the entitlement's unit.

licenseTier.description: Whether the seats were bought or granted.

licenseStatus.description: Current lifecycle state of the seats.

nextLifecycleStatus.description: State the seats move to next if nothing changes -- typically `Warning` at the renewal date, then `Suspended`.

nextLifecycleDate.description: When `nextLifecycleStatus` takes effect. Returned as `0001-01-01T00:00:00` -- .NET's `DateTime.MinValue` -- when no transition is scheduled. Note this sentinel carries no timezone designator, unlike every other timestamp on this API.

EntitlementPayGo.description: The pay-as-you-go side of an entitlement: consumption billed to a billing policy's Azure subscription rather than drawn from licensed capacity. A tenant with no billing policy still gets this block, with zeroes.

entitled.description: Pay-as-you-go allowance. Observed as zero throughout; pay-as-you-go is uncapped, so this is not a ceiling.

EntitlementProductView.description: The same entitlement record as `Entitlement`, in the v0.1-alpha representation. Beyond the flattened capacity block, note `unit` moves from the entitlement to inside `capacity`, and `Hour` appears here as a unit where v2.0 reports `Count` for the same meter.

message.description: Human-readable reason, quoting the rejected value.

target.description: Name of the route parameter or field that failed. The only machine-actionable pointer any error envelope on this host provides.

KeyMessageError.description: A bare JSON array of key/message pairs -- neither of the object envelopes. Returned on a 404 from `Entitlements/{entitlementId}` when the id is not a value the entitlement subsystem recognises. A client must test the top-level JSON type before reading any error on this host.

message.description: Free text that interpolates the rejected value and the tenant id.

LicenseQuantityBreakdown.description: How many licence seats of a kind are in each lifecycle state. The three add up to the seats purchased; only `enabled` seats contribute capacity.

warning.description: Seats past their renewal date but still inside the grace period -- capacity they granted is still honoured but will lapse.

suspended.description: Seats past the grace period. They no longer grant capacity.

LicensingPrincipal.description: Whoever created or last changed a record. Only the directory object id and its kind are given; no display name, mail address or tenant is returned, so resolving the principal takes a Microsoft Graph call.

id.description: Entra directory object id of the principal.

type.x-enum-evidence: Only `User` was observed. Service principals almost certainly appear here as another value, so this is deliberately not an `enum`.

ODataServiceDocument.description: The vestigial OData service document at the host root. `value` was empty and `@odata.context` pointed at an internal cluster address on a private IP -- not a URL a caller can or should follow.

@odata.context.description: Points at an internal service endpoint rather than a public one. Do not dereference.

PayGoEntitlement.description: One product meter's pay-as-you-go switch inside a v2.0 billing policy. The array is exhaustive: every meter the policy could cover is listed whether or not it is switched on, so absence from the array means the meter is not supported rather than not enabled.

entitlementId.description: The metered resource this switch governs.
entitlementId.x-enum-evidence: Both policies in the probed tenant listed exactly these eleven ids in full. Note this vocabulary is *not* the same as the one the `Entitlements/{entitlementId}` route accepts -- see that operation.

productCategory.description: Which Power Platform product the meter belongs to.
productCategory.x-enum-evidence: The six categories spanned by the exhaustive entitlement list above.

payAsYouGoState.description: Whether overage on this meter is billed to the policy's Azure subscription. `false` means overage is blocked instead. This is the boolean the v0.1-alpha representation writes as an `Enabled`/`Disabled` string.

value.description: Ceiling on pay-as-you-go spend for this meter, in the meter's own unit. The observed value in every case was `1.7976931348623157e308` -- IEEE-754 `Double.MaxValue`, the service's sentinel for *no ceiling*. A finite value here would be a real cap; treat the sentinel as unlimited rather than as a number.

PowerAutomatePayAsYouGoPolicy.description: Pay-as-you-go state for Power Automate, which -- unlike every other product family -- splits into three independently switchable meters.

cloudFlowRunsPayAsYouGoState.description: Billing for cloud flow runs beyond the licensed allowance.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9110 problem details. Returned on a 404 from a route that exists but whose bound id has no record.

traceId.description: ASP.NET Core connection and request id. It identifies the request inside the service's own logs but is not a support-facing correlation id; use the `x-ms-correlation-id` response header for that.

ProductPayAsYouGoPolicy.description: Pay-as-you-go state for one product family in the v0.1-alpha representation.

payAsYouGoState.description: Whether overage for this product is billed to the policy's Azure subscription.
payAsYouGoState.x-enum-evidence: Both values observed live in one response (`storagePolicy` Enabled, the rest Disabled).

Quantity.description: A boxed scalar. The v2.0 representation wraps quantities in an object where v0.1-alpha returns a bare number.

ServiceFabricError.description: Service Fabric fault envelope, returned as a 500 when a route parameter cannot be bound at all. It carries no message, no trace id and no detail, so there is nothing to act on but the status code.

TenantCapacity.description: The tenant's complete capacity position: an overall verdict plus one entry per metered resource.

tenantId.description: Echoes the tenant id from the path.

licenseModelType.description: Which licensing model the tenant is on, which determines how entitlement is computed -- `StorageDriven` tenants get capacity from storage grants rather than per-user allowances.

tenantCapacities.description: One entry per metered resource, always the full set.

TenantCapacityMeter.description: One metered resource in the tenant capacity rollup, with its entitlement broken into layers and its consumption snapshot.

capacityType.description: The metered resource. `Database`/`File`/`Log` are the three Dataverse storage meters; the `Trial`, `SubscriptionTrial` and `M365` prefixes are the same resources granted by trial, subscription-trial and Microsoft 365 seeded licences respectively and are tracked separately because they expire independently; `ApiCallCount` is the Power Platform request allowance; `FinOps` meters cover Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations storage.
capacityType.x-enum-evidence: All sixteen were returned in a single tenant's rollup; the service emits every meter it models regardless of entitlement, so this is the full set as of 2026-08.

capacityUnits.description: Unit for every quantity on this meter. `Unit` is a dimensionless count (environments, API calls); `None` is emitted for meters the tenant has no entitlement to at all.

totalCapacity.description: Sum of the meter's entitlement layers.

maxCapacity.description: Hard ceiling for the meter. Returned as `0` for every meter observed, including meters with non-zero `totalCapacity`, so it does not mean what its name suggests and should not be read as a limit.

status.description: Per-meter health. `NotAvailable` means consumption exceeds entitlement -- environment operations that need this resource will be refused. `None` means the meter is not in play for this tenant.

overflowCapacity.description: Capacity borrowed from elsewhere to cover overage. Frequently empty.

Trial.description: A per-user product trial with its currency allowances, as returned under the `v1.0` segment.

trialType.description: Which trial. Echoes the path, normalised to canonical casing.
trialType.x-enum-evidence: `AI` is the only value the route accepts; fifteen other plausible product names were each rejected with 400 InvalidValue.

startDate.description: When the trial was activated for this user.

expiryDate.description: When it lapses. A past date means the trial is over; expired trials are still returned rather than omitted, so a caller must compare against the current time itself.

trialCurrencyUnits.description: Currency allowances the trial granted. Absent from the v0.1-alpha representation.

trialCount.description: How many times this user has taken this trial. Absent from the v0.1-alpha representation.

TrialCurrencyUnit.description: One currency granted by a trial, with the allowance and how much of it the user has spent.

trialUnits.description: Units granted for the life of the trial.

trialConsumedUnits.description: Units spent. The trial is exhausted when this reaches `trialUnits`, independently of `expiryDate`.

TrialDatesOnly.description: The same trial record as `Trial`, in the v0.1-alpha representation: dates only. `trialCurrencyUnits` and `trialCount` are omitted, so a caller that needs the remaining allowance must use the `v1.0` segment.

ValidationError.description: Nested error envelope with per-field details, returned on a 400 when a path segment fails enum binding.

message.example: One or more errors found. See 'Details' field for more information
